gen-dafont-upheaval-fs-ranade: Bold and tight-throated up top, Upheaval packs tall sturdy letters with gaps between them, while Ranade spreads out with open stroke ends. Ranade's slightly stretchy weight keeps a long paragraph moving easily.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-fs-familjen-grot: Fixed-width, code-style letters with a towering x-height give VCR OSD Mono its lo-fi, retro-tech look. Familjen Grotesk follows with sans-serif bowls left open on one side, and it gets more lively when you give it a little extra size.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-gf-cascadia-code: A towering x-height and fixed-width, code-style letters make VCR OSD Mono feel like an old screen overlay. And Cascadia Code adds a wire-thin sans with generous gaps between neighbors, so the two read as modern against retro.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-switzer: Lo-fi and a bit retro-tech, VCR OSD Mono sets the mood with its towering, fixed-width letters. Switzer, a plain sans with wire-like forms and a tall waist line, is the one built for steady reading, where the heading is built for effect.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-bespoke-slab: Verve brings approachable sans lettering with trimmed side bearings and bowls that nearly close, thick strokes sitting beside hair-thin ones. And Bespoke Slab, a serif with tall lowercase bodies, is the grounded one, better at carrying the text than grabbing the eye.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-alpino: Alpino is cozy and casual, with tall bodies that make its ascenders look short. Visitor's gaping e mouths and solder-thin strokes bring the nostalgic digital flavor, so a modest bump in Alpino's size would keep that plain sans comfortable beside it.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-fira-sans: Gaping mouths on the e and strokes pulled like solder make Visitor instantly nostalgic and digital. Fira Sans brings clean, wide-open s curves and a large x-height, and that gap in personality is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Retro pixel-era charm, up front. Visitor is best at that nostalgic digital punch with its big bowls and short ascenders, while Noto Sans Lisu does the quieter job of staying tidy, with wide-open s curves and tiny gaps under its ascender tops.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-roboto: Roboto brings generous round mouths and a modest drop from capital to lowercase height, which sits well beside Visitor's drafting-pen outlines. Nudge Roboto's size up a touch.
gen-dafont-visitor-work-sans: Work Sans is contemporary and modern, with c tips that never creep toward touching and a mean line set high, under Visitor's gaping e. Over many lines it reads smoothly.
